- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +2.0+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% to account for mean reversion.
- If model consistently forecasts below true outcome in early days of 30d horizon, it’s underestimating momentum — add 0.5–1.0 to first 3–5 forecasted days.
- When sentiment is neutral or positive (e.g., > 0.5), model often underestimates upside — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 in early days if sentiment is trending up.
- Model frequently lags in capturing sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after day 10, adjust forecast to rise 0.5–1.0 per day for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak, price drops 5–10%), model often overpredicts — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 in those days.
- For 30d horizon, if model’s first 5 days are consistently below true, apply a “warm-up” bias: add 0.3–0.7 to first 5 forecasted days to capture early momentum.
